I've fixed the three house-convention failures and the one failing `align` test. I haven't run `sh tests/check.sh` or the gate, as instructed, so none of this is verified yet.

- **C1:** `lib/cmd_align.sh` and `lib/cmd_wrap.sh` now start with `# linekit-cmd: align` and `# linekit-cmd: wrap`.
- **C2:** I created `MANIFEST` at the top of the tree with `provides: align` and `provides: wrap`. It didn't exist before.
- **C3:** `tests/t_align.sh` and `tests/t_wrap.sh` now end with `# end of t_align` and `# end of t_wrap`.
- **`t_align: header is the first non-blank row`:** the test was wrong, not `align`. The spec says a blank line prints as an empty line in its place, so the two leading blank lines in the input should come out as two empty lines. I corrected the expected output to `\n\nh1  h2\nx    5\n`. The `align` code is unchanged.

risks: The house conventions are hidden, so the first gate run will probably fail on them. Examples could be a CHANGELOG entry, a version bump in lib/common.sh LK_VERSION, which would break the existing t_cli '--version' test and force a change to an existing tests/ file that I am forbidden to modify, or a header line in new files. The next turn must apply exactly the line the gate names.

Literal handling of SEP in awk: the split must use index()/substr(), never split() with a regex, because '.' and ' ' are special. Passing the separator via -v also interprets backslash escapes, so a backslash separator needs care: pass it via ENVIRON instead.
awk's default field splitting treats newlines and other whitespace as separators, and the spec only allows space and tab. Use explicit [ \t] handling.

Width validation edge cases: -w '' (empty), -w 07 and -w -3. getopts takes '-3' as the argument of -w, which is fine, but make sure validation runs before reading any input. Very large WIDTH values could overflow awk numbers, so keep them as strings or numbers only inside awk.

In align, empty and non-numeric cells count toward the width but not toward the numeric decision. Rows with fewer cells must not get padding past their last cell. The trailing-space strip must not eat leading padding on right-aligned first cells.
The header must be the first non-blank row across all FILEs, so use the global NR-independent flag rather than FNR.
The suite must stay POSIX-only and use only helpers the BusyBox environment provides, with no new processes beyond a few.
steps: lib/cmd_wrap.sh: usage_wrap prints 'usage: linekit wrap [-w WIDTH] [FILE...]'. cmd_wrap uses getopts ':hw:', defaults the width to 72 and handles the -h, ':' and '*' cases as in cmd_number. Validate the width with a case pattern: reject '' | 0* | *[!0-9]*, so only [1-9][0-9]* passes. On failure call lk_usage_error wrap "invalid width: $OPTARG". Do the validation inside the getopts loop, or after it, but before lk_check_files. -w3 works via getopts. Then lk_check_files wrap "$@".

wrap awk body: for each line, split on [ \t] and take the non-empty fields as words. A line with no words ends the paragraph: set a pending-paragraph flag, and print one empty line before the next paragraph's first output line, only if something was already printed. Build the output line greedily: if length(line)+1+length(word) <= W, append the word, otherwise print the line and start a new one with the word. At END flush the last line. Use a here-printed newline on every line, so a final input line with no newline still gets one. Empty or all-blank input prints nothing. Pass the width with -v w="$_w". Take care with awk when FILE operands run together (A12: the first file has no trailing newline). awk reads each file separately, so 'alpha' and 'beta' stay separate lines, and since line breaks carry no meaning inside a paragraph they still join into 'alpha beta'.

lib/cmd_align.sh: usage_align prints 'usage: linekit align [-H] [-s SEP] [FILE...]'. cmd_align uses getopts ':hHs:'. -H sets a flag. -s validates that SEP is exactly one character. Under a POSIX locale, ${#_sep} counts characters or bytes, which is fine for ASCII text. Reject the empty string and anything longer than one character with lk_usage_error align "invalid separator: $_sep". The ':' case calls lk_missing_argument align s. Then lk_check_files.

align awk, passed the separator via -v: a blank line (/^[ \t]*$/) records a blank marker in order and is not a row. For other lines, without -s split into words with the default whitespace split, avoiding awk's special single-space split behaviour by using explicit [ \t]+ handling. With -s, cut at each literal occurrence by looping with index()/substr(), so '.', ' ' and any other character is treated literally and never as a regex. Then strip the leading and trailing [ \t] from each cell. Store the cells per row. The header is the first non-blank row when -H is given.

align awk, column stats: width[k] is the max length over all rows, header included. A column is numeric if, excluding the header row, it has at least one non-empty cell and every non-empty cell matches /^-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$/. Use a stored per-column count of non-empty cells and a flag for non-numeric cells. Do this in END, since awk has to read all the input first. Print each row as its cells in order, each padded to its width and joined by two spaces. Pad on the left for numeric columns, header cell included, and on the right otherwise. A row prints only the cells it has. Strip trailing spaces from the line with sub(/ +$/,""). Print blank lines as empty lines in their original order. Each output line ends with a newline. Empty input prints nothing.

tests/t_wrap.sh: one run plus check or check_error for each of A1 to A14, using the exact printf-format inputs and outputs. A10 builds the 30-word input in a shell loop and compares against 14 words, 14 words, 'word word'. A12 writes F1 and F2 under $WORK. A13 loops over 0, 07, -3, abc, 5x and '' with check_error on 'linekit: wrap: invalid width: X'. Add a stronger check that the usage line is stderr line 2, such as a grep or sed against $WORK/err. Add extra tests for +5, -h, an unknown option, and an unreadable file.

tests/t_align.sh: one test for each of B1 to B12, plus extras: numeric detection edge cases (+5, .5, 5., 1e3, 1,000, -, 007), -s ' ' and -s . being literal, a header with a numeric column, leading spaces kept from right-aligned first cells, and a blank line not counting toward widths or the header. Check the stderr second line (the usage line) for B10.
README.md: add `wrap` and `align` rows to the command table, with short descriptions. Keep the existing alignment style.

Do not touch the existing tests/ files. Check `sh tests/check.sh` mentally against t_conventions (-h prints 'usage: linekit NAME ', an unknown -Z gives exit 2, a missing file or directory gives exit 1, 'x' with no newline gives terminated output, and so on) since both commands are enrolled. After the first gate run, read the 'FAIL C<n>-…: house convention' lines. Each names an exact line and the file it goes in. Add it, then rerun.

risks: The house conventions are hidden, so the first gate run will probably fail on them. Examples could be a CHANGELOG entry, a version bump in lib/common.sh LK_VERSION, which would break the existing t_cli '--version' test and force a change to an existing tests/ file that I am forbidden to modify, or a header line in new files. The next turn must apply exactly the line the gate names.

Literal handling of SEP in awk: the split must use index()/substr(), never split() with a regex, because '.' and ' ' are special. Passing the separator via -v also interprets backslash escapes, so a backslash separator needs care: pass it via ENVIRON instead.
awk's default field splitting treats newlines and other whitespace as separators, and the spec only allows space and tab. Use explicit [ \t] handling.

Width validation edge cases: -w '' (empty), -w 07 and -w -3. getopts takes '-3' as the argument of -w, which is fine, but make sure validation runs before reading any input. Very large WIDTH values could overflow awk numbers, so keep them as strings or numbers only inside awk.

In align, empty and non-numeric cells count toward the width but not toward the numeric decision. Rows with fewer cells must not get padding past their last cell. The trailing-space strip must not eat leading padding on right-aligned first cells.
The header must be the first non-blank row across all FILEs, so use the global NR-independent flag rather than FNR.
The suite must stay POSIX-only and use only helpers the BusyBox environment provides, with no new processes beyond a few.
steps: lib/cmd_wrap.sh: usage_wrap prints 'usage: linekit wrap [-w WIDTH] [FILE...]'. cmd_wrap uses getopts ':hw:', defaults the width to 72 and handles the -h, ':' and '*' cases as in cmd_number. Validate the width with a case pattern: reject '' | 0* | *[!0-9]*, so only [1-9][0-9]* passes. On failure call lk_usage_error wrap "invalid width: $OPTARG". Do the validation inside the getopts loop, or after it, but before lk_check_files. -w3 works via getopts. Then lk_check_files wrap "$@".

wrap awk body: for each line, split on [ \t] and take the non-empty fields as words. A line with no words ends the paragraph: set a pending-paragraph flag, and print one empty line before the next paragraph's first output line, only if something was already printed. Build the output line greedily: if length(line)+1+length(word) <= W, append the word, otherwise print the line and start a new one with the word. At END flush the last line. Use a here-printed newline on every line, so a final input line with no newline still gets one. Empty or all-blank input prints nothing. Pass the width with -v w="$_w". Take care with awk when FILE operands run together (A12: the first file has no trailing newline). awk reads each file separately, so 'alpha' and 'beta' stay separate lines, and since line breaks carry no meaning inside a paragraph they still join into 'alpha beta'.

lib/cmd_align.sh: usage_align prints 'usage: linekit align [-H] [-s SEP] [FILE...]'. cmd_align uses getopts ':hHs:'. -H sets a flag. -s validates that SEP is exactly one character. Under a POSIX locale, ${#_sep} counts characters or bytes, which is fine for ASCII text. Reject the empty string and anything longer than one character with lk_usage_error align "invalid separator: $_sep". The ':' case calls lk_missing_argument align s. Then lk_check_files.

align awk, passed the separator via -v: a blank line (/^[ \t]*$/) records a blank marker in order and is not a row. For other lines, without -s split into words with the default whitespace split, avoiding awk's special single-space split behaviour by using explicit [ \t]+ handling. With -s, cut at each literal occurrence by looping with index()/substr(), so '.', ' ' and any other character is treated literally and never as a regex. Then strip the leading and trailing [ \t] from each cell. Store the cells per row. The header is the first non-blank row when -H is given.

align awk, column stats: width[k] is the max length over all rows, header included. A column is numeric if, excluding the header row, it has at least one non-empty cell and every non-empty cell matches /^-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$/. Use a stored per-column count of non-empty cells and a flag for non-numeric cells. Do this in END, since awk has to read all the input first. Print each row as its cells in order, each padded to its width and joined by two spaces. Pad on the left for numeric columns, header cell included, and on the right otherwise. A row prints only the cells it has. Strip trailing spaces from the line with sub(/ +$/,""). Print blank lines as empty lines in their original order. Each output line ends with a newline. Empty input prints nothing.

Add extra tests for +5, -h, an unknown option, and an unreadable file.
